newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Hypobank says 96 loss still a good result.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Hypobank says 96 loss still a good result.

text.p: Hypo-Bank Slovakia a.s., a wholly-owned subsidiary of German Bayerische Hypotheken-und Wechsel-Bank AG, said on Friday it posted a net loss of 67 million crowns in 1996.

"We planned a loss of around 190 million crowns so in this light the results may be considered as good," Karl-L. Wiedemann, Hypo-Bank Slovakia Chairman of the Board of Directors, told a news conference.
Wiedemann said the bank's balance sum totalled 1.55 billion crowns at the end of last year, adding it has been gradually rising this year to 2.21 billion as of April 10.

Hypo-Bank Slovakia said it had applied for a licence to expand its activities to securities trading and to providing mortage services. "We hope that we will recieve a mortage licence in 1998 and that we could start this service soon afterwards," Wiedemann said.
This, however, will require an increase of the bank's basic capital to at least one billion crowns, which, Wiedemann said, will happen in the near future. He did not elaborate.

The bank plans to cover part of its Slovak actvities by bond issues, which can include domestic paper, international bonds denominated in crowns or, for special client activities, foreign currencies, said bank board member Martin Horsky.
But, he said it was still too early to give any further information on the plan.
Outgoing chairman of the supervisory board, Hans H. Friedl, said Hypo-Bank planned to double its Hungarian network to 16 branches by the end of 1998.
He added that expansion in the Czech Republic, where the bank now operates 16 branches and four representative offices, was completed.
"We have also applied for approval for conversion of our Moscow office to a wholly-owned daughter bank, and we hope to get this licence by the end of this year," Friedl said.
